clue.text: Look, RAC's fixed holes in boat!

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or tampered with, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the motoring organisation's initials with the S, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone points out that the breakdown service has patched the holes in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British roadside-recovery service, which makes 'fixed' read as a repair job rather than a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarlocks are the rowing fittings, often notches or rings in the gunwale, where oars rest while a crew pulls.

clue.text: Buddhist temple accommodating land animal that's considered semi-aquatic

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to a guest, so one piece is housed within another

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
Latin for land, as in terra firma

explanation.surface: A Thai temple puts up a creature that lives half in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land animal' looks like one phrase, but the split falls after 'land'; the animal belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The water rat, or water vole, is a rodent that swims and lives along riverbanks, spending time both ashore and afloat.

clue.text: Dog and what it may do without a lead possibly?

indicators.note: 'without' means lacking, so a single letter is dropped from the word nearby
'possibly' offers one of several ways the letters could be arranged

blocks.note: a dog may foul the pavement, which is what owners must clean up
a dog's leash, taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog, and the mess it might make when let off its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'lead' the leash a dog walks on, but it is only letters: lose the A, then mix what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is a curly-coated breed of dog, so the single word names it directly as an example.

clue.text: Covering up not criminal case? Having more to say

indicators.note: a case is an outer shell, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
'not' says these letters must be absent from the longer word

blocks.note: cladding is a protective outer layer put on a building
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A cover-up, and a criminal case where someone still has more to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal case' looks like a legal case; it is the shell of 'criminal', CL, removed from the front of CLADDING.
explanation.definitionFit: When a speaker is adding, they are continuing with further remarks, which is having extra words to offer.

clue.text: Line up on left coming back, he cries

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
coming back is returning the way one came, so the order is reversed

blocks.note: a ley is a line, as in ley lines across a landscape
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone lines up on the left, returning, and shouts out.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate reversals: LEY goes up to YEL, then RE plus L comes back as LER. 'He cries' is the definition, a person who yells.
explanation.definitionFit: A yeller is someone who shouts loudly, so the phrase describing a man who cries out names that person.

clue.text: Alan resolved to maintain a bit of defiance - a court winner

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it down and settle it differently, so the letters are reworked
to maintain is to keep and hold, so these letters hold another inside them
a small bit is just one letter, taken from the start of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man called Alan is determined to keep defying, the mark of a champion in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court; Rafael Nadal is the Spanish player with a record number of French Open titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafael Nadal won many Grand Slam tennis titles, so he is a famous victor on the tennis court.

clue.text: Group (as a whole) about to get ill-gotten gains

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about with dates
boodle is slang for money obtained by bribery or theft

explanation.surface: A gang, taken together, is on the point of collecting its loot.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hints at the idiom 'the whole caboodle', where the word means the entire lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A caboodle is a collection or lot of things or people, chiefly heard in the idiom meaning everything together.

clue.text: Article on German director Lee

blocks.note: the indefinite article
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a German film-maker named Lee.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second, so AN sits over G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ang Lee is the Taiwanese film-maker behind Brokeback Mountain and Life of Pi, so his first name completes the phrase.

clue.text: Visited Ivy with a drug-smuggling solicitor?

indicators.note: smugglers hide goods inside something, so one piece is concealed within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a tout solicits custom, for example selling tickets
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A trip to see Ivy alongside a lawyer who smuggles drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy reads like a woman's name, but The Ivy is a famous London restaurant. 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer; here it is someone touting for business.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to a restaurant for a meal is eating out, so visiting a well-known one fits the phrase as an example.

clue.text: Mostly stolen, deficit's original solution for the most senior

indicators.note: 'mostly' means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
the original of something comes first, so the opening letter is taken
a solution is something dissolved and remixed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Money mostly stolen, and the eldest are given the first way out of the shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' reads as an answer to the deficit, but it signals mixing the letters of STOLE and D.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior person in a group is the one with greatest age, so the superlative matches exactly.

clue.text: One in supreme role's worse reportedly - a monster

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the supreme being is God, and worse in health is iller; said together the phrase runs into the monster's name

explanation.surface: Someone in the top job is said to be getting worse: a real monster.
explanation.walkthrough: GOD'S ILLER said quickly gives the name of the Japanese film monster; 'worse' is taken as more ill, not as more bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Godzilla is the giant reptilian creature from Japanese films, a famous example of a movie beast.

clue.text: PO 'crime' clear to a lunatic

indicators.note: a lunatic behaves wildly, so the letters are thrown into a crazy new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Post Office's 'crime' is obvious to anyone, however unhinged.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the PO (Post Office) Horizon scandal, where postmasters were wrongly prosecuted, is cast as wrongdoing by an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate malice is wrongful intent attributed to a company, which is how many see the Post Office's pursuit of innocent sub-postmasters.

clue.text: In accordance with tricky parse

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and not straightforward, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Following the rules of a difficult grammatical analysis.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in accordance with' as a grammar instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used in instructions meaning following or according to, as in following the manual.

clue.text: Female in fix over first of losses

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the letters run backwards
the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to rig is to fix a result dishonestly
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman in trouble over the first of her losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fix' looks like 'in a jam', but 'in' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a young female person, so the general term covers it as a simple synonym.

clue.text: Language based on Esperanto is one and the same

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: An artificial tongue derived from another is described as identical to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One and the same' reads as an idiom, but it splits into two pieces joined by 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is a constructed international language created in 1907 as a reformed offshoot of an earlier planned tongue.

clue.text: Need a word quietly - Second Sight not content

indicators.note: the content of a word is its middle, so without it only the outside letters remain

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
S is the abbreviation for second
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A quiet request for a chat with a clairvoyant who is not happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like happy, but here it is the inside of a word, removed to leave its shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hushed sound used to catch someone's attention discreetly when you want to talk privately.

clue.text: Reach not the last resort

indicators.note: 'not the last' tells you to leave off the final letter

blocks.note: the reach of a bridge or an outstretched hand is the distance it covers

explanation.surface: Arriving somewhere other than a place of final desperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last resort' is a phrase, but 'the last' belongs to the wordplay and 'resort' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a health resort with mineral springs or treatments, so it is an example of a holiday destination.

clue.text: Operation controlled by thugs in suits from the outset ... and hats

indicators.note: something controlled is held in check, so it sits inside the controlling letters
the outset is the start, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of the three words
op is short for a surgical or military operation

explanation.surface: A racket run by suited heavies from the start, with headgear on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis holds back the definition to the very end; topis are sun helmets, known also as pith helmets.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a lightweight sun helmet worn in hot countries, so the plural names a kind of headgear.

clue.text: Disdainful having set up extremely nervous suspect

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom
the extremes of a word are its two ends

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
iffy is informal for dubious or suspect

explanation.surface: Someone scornful has framed a very jumpy suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' suggests framing someone, but in a down clue it reverses the letters; 'suspect' is an adjective, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sniffy means looking down on things with contempt, the same scornful attitude as being haughty.

clue.text: Purpose of prison: reforming those inside?

indicators.note: reforming means reshaping, and it applies only to the inner letters while the ends stay put

blocks.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail

explanation.surface: Asking what jail is for: is it rehabilitating its inmates?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those inside' sounds like prisoners, but it means the middle letters of the word, which swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or objective, something one sets out to achieve, so it shares the sense of intention.

clue.text: Pull up and give lift to Frenchman who may be a pro in bed

definitions.text: who may be a pro in bed

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards
lifting raises something, which in a down clue turns it to read upwards

blocks.note: to drag is to pull along
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Stopping the car to give a ride to a Frenchman who could be a professional lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition suggests a gigolo, but the bed is a flower bed and the pro works in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional horticulturist tends plants in borders and flower beds, so an expert there is someone growing plants for a living.

clue.text: After fracas, Keane not starting - best he's not there

indicators.note: after a fracas everything is in disarray, so the letters end up scrambled
'not starting' tells you to remove the opening letter

blocks.note: the name without its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a brawl, Keane is dropped from the line-up, so the best player is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Roy Keane, the combative former Manchester United captain, and George Best make a football scene, but both names are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is a person who is missing from where they are expected, so the phrase describes him well.

clue.text: How to refer to Queen (introductions to Meghan Markle are repeatedly blocked)

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so each word gives its opening letter
something blocked in is hemmed in on both sides, so the letters sit between others

blocks.note: the initial letters of the two names
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A, here taken twice

explanation.surface: Royal etiquette: how to address the monarch, with Meghan's introductions repeatedly stalled.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal protocol has the Queen addressed as Ma'am after the first greeting; the apostrophe is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ma'am is the formal term of address used to speak to a queen after first calling her Your Majesty.

clue.text: Body part in bird (adult) is arc-shaped

indicators.note: to shape something is to mould it into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anatomical feature of a grown bird that curves like a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arc-shaped' reads as one description, but the hyphen hides 'arc' as fodder and 'shaped' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds have air sacs linked to the lungs that store air and help breathing during flight, so it is an avian organ.

clue.text: See 12
Mark hanging round to enjoy celebration

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for the German mark
an arras is a tapestry wall hanging
to dig something is slang for liking it

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark hangs about to make the most of a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name, and 'hanging round' like loitering, but the hanging is a tapestry and Mark is a currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the carnival festival held on Shrove Tuesday, famous in New Orleans, so it is a festive occasion.

clue.text: In backtracking secures American capital

indicators.note: 'in' tells you the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
to backtrack is to retrace one's steps, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Backpedalling in order to secure an American capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American' suggests a US city, but it only supplies letters; the capital is in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Maseru is the capital city of Lesotho, the mountain kingdom surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Puritans, having lost money, becoming deaf teachers

indicators.note: what has been lost is gone, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: moralists are strict preachers of right conduct, like puritans
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Strict puritans lose their money and turn to teaching deaf pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deaf teachers' sounds like teachers who cannot hear; it means those who teach the deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Oralists teach deaf people through speech and lip-reading rather than signing, so they are instructors of deaf students.

clue.text: With leaders twisted, taken advantage of and prosecuted

indicators.note: twisting the leading letters swaps their order while the rest stays as it is

blocks.note: to be used is to be exploited

explanation.surface: Someone who was exploited and then hauled into court.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters swap; the leaders are opening letters, not people in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring legal proceedings against someone, close to the idea of taking them to court.

clue.text: Working with slave around Californian city

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on
a serf was a feudal bonded labourer

explanation.surface: Labouring with a slave somewhere in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but here it turns the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresno is a large city in California's Central Valley, an example of a West Coast urban centre.

clue.text: Considered guilty, resistance suppressed and condemned

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down and kept in, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: the accused is the person charged with a crime
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A defendant is presumed guilty, opposition is crushed, and he is sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Considered guilty' is wordplay rather than the definition: it is how the accused are wrongly treated before trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accursed is under a curse or doomed, which matches being damned or sentenced to ruin.

clue.text: Desert surprisingly green, very - that's not right?

indicators.note: a surprising result comes out unexpectedly, so the letters land in an unforeseen order
'not right' asks for the letter standing for right to be removed

blocks.note: the word without its R
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A desert that is unexpectedly lush: surely that can't be correct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' could be a verb meaning abandon; here it is the noun, a dry region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Negev is the arid region covering southern Israel, so it is an example of a dry wilderness.
